pathogen.value: Aviadenovirus (avian adenovirus), several species with the most common serogroups being 1, 2 and 3

value: mainly through droppings contaminating feed, water or environment
serogroup 1 can also pass from hen to chick through the egg
can stay dormant in an infected bird and flare up when the bird is stressed
anemia and dehydration in gut infections
eggs of abnormal size, shape, colour or texture

diagnosis.value: Lab testing is needed, including tissue examination, electron microscopy, virus isolation, ELISA and PCR; a drop in egg production can be confirmed with a specific antibody test

value: vaccines exist for haemorrhagic enteritis and egg drop syndrome

treatment_overview.value: No specific treatment mentioned beyond reducing stress, hygiene and nutrition to lower the chance of clinical disease

summary.value: Avian adenovirus is a group of related viruses found worldwide that can cause gut, reproductive or organ disease in chickens and other poultry, often staying hidden until a bird is stressed. Vaccines exist for some forms, and management focuses on hygiene, nutrition and reducing stress rather than direct treatment.
